sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Selections let your programs make decisions—just like you do every day! Here’s what we’ll cover:

• How to use `if` statements to choose different actions
• Ways to handle multiple conditions with `else` and `else if`
• How to avoid common mistakes that trip up beginners

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how selections work:

steps.title: Check Condition
steps.description: The program evaluates a condition (like `radius < 0`). This is like asking: "Is the radius negative?"

steps.title: Take Action
steps.description: If the condition is true, the code inside the `if` block runs. If false, it skips or goes to `else`.

steps.title: Alternative Path
steps.description: With `else`, the program has a backup plan. If the condition is false, it executes the `else` block.

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Selections = decision-making in code (like a flowchart)
✓ `if` checks a condition—if true, it runs the code inside
✓ `else` gives a fallback option when the condition is false
✓ Indentation matters for readability (but doesn’t affect execution)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Indent your code inside `if`/`else` blocks for clarity
Test all possible paths (true *and* false conditions)
donts: Forget the curly braces `{}` for multi-line blocks
Assume `else` is optional—it’s not always needed!
sections.protip: Use `else if` to chain multiple conditions neatly. It’s cleaner than nested `if` statements!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Selections are everywhere in real apps! Here’s how they’re used:

examples.how: Checks if username/password match. If true, grants access; else, shows an error.
Uses selections to apply discounts: "If cart total > $100, apply 10% off."
Decides what happens when a player collides with an object: "If player touches coin, add points."

sections.title: 🧪 Practice Problem
sections.content: Try this challenge: Write a program that checks if a number is positive, negative, or zero.

problem.description:
Create a program that asks the user for a number and prints:
- "Positive" if the number is > 0
- "Negative" if the number is < 0
- "Zero" if the number is 0
hints: Use `if`, `else if`, and `else` to cover all cases
Remember: `0` is neither positive nor negative!
problem.explanation: The program checks the number in order: first for positivity, then negativity, and defaults to zero if neither condition is met. This covers all possible cases!

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Selections let your program make decisions using `if`, `else if`, and `else`
📌 Practice writing conditions for real-world scenarios (like login checks)
📌 Ready for next topic: combining conditions with logical operators!
